messages:
jess-cs: Hey team, ExampleCorp says traffic from several EU customers is getting routed to our us-west cluster and they see 1500-3000ms p50 + intermittent 401s. Started ~0900 UTC. Can someone triage?

maria-support: Thanks Jess — I grabbed the customer logs. They show X-Request-Region: eu-west but our backend saw region=us-west and token validation failed once the request hit the wrong auth pool.

alan-netops: Possible NAT64 / ISP HTTP proxy rewriting client IPs. I saw their ISP (NetBridge) in past cause EDNS client-subnet to be stripped and add a transparent proxy.

sam-eng: Repro steps from customer?

jess-cs: They ran: 
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "X-Client-IP: 82.31.45.12" \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
They also provided a dig showing our A record resolves to a us-west anycast IP from their resolver.

kyra-sre: Can we get a packet capture or the resolver chain? I asked customer for `dig +short @resolver example.com` and `dig +trace example.com` — waiting. In the meantime I'll check our edge logs for client IP and EDNS info.

alan-netops: Quick check in edge logs: I found a cluster of requests around 09:07 with no edns-client-subnet and source IPs from NetBridge NAT pool (82.31.0.0/16). They landed on us-west because our GeoIP lookup saw the proxy IP mapped to US.

sam-eng: That explains latency. What about the 401s?

maria-support: 401s correlate with requests that hit our us-west auth pool where the customer's token is not yet replicated (they're on EU-only project). Token lookup hits returned 403/401 before fallback worked. Billing also recorded a few full-charge attempts in us-west — customer flagged duplicate billing lines.

kyra-sre: Plan: 1) Add a temporary routing rule to prefer EU for requests with X-Client-IP in their ASN / known NAT ranges. 2) Patch edge to use original-client-ip header when present (we already accept X-Forwarded-For but not this custom) 3) Long-term: add NAT/proxy heuristics to GeoIP and require EDNS client-subnet fallback to ask resolver for subnet.

sam-eng: For repro: I can simulate with iptables SNAT via a proxy VM in our lab, and run `dig +edns=0` vs `dig +edns=1` to show resolver behavior. Also will run our internal load test to ensure fallback policy doesn't route too many extra requests to EU.

jess-cs: Customer agreed to a quick DNS TTL flush and to test from a different resolver (8.8.8.8). They said using 8.8.8.8 returned eu-west IP and latency dropped to 45ms.

maria-support: Escalating to Ops and Billing: please note affected timeframe 09:00-09:18 UTC, customer org ID 8742 — they want a billing adjustment for duplicate entries and confirmation once routing rule is applied.

alan-netops: I'll open a change with a short-lived route rule and post the change ID here. Expected ETA 20m.

deploy-bot: Change queued: CHG-2026-3345 — routing rule to prefer EU for NetBridge ASN ranges. Scheduled at 09:44 UTC.

kyra-sre: Follow-ups: need a permanent solution to identify transparent proxies (NAT64/NAT44) and prefer edns-client-subnet when present. I'll add an RFC for next sprint. Also will add a metric to surface client IP mismatch rate.

jess-cs: I'll update the customer once CHG-2026-3345 is applied and confirm billing remediation. Thanks all :thumbsup:
